clue.text: Petty quarrel with some New York jeweller

parts.note: a tiff is a minor squabble
as in 'have you got any?'

explanation.surface: A minor row breaks out with a fashionable Manhattan jeweller.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffany & Co. is the famous jewellery firm with its flagship store on Fifth Avenue in New York.

clue.text: Ambassador taken in by right-wing supposition

indicators.note: being taken in means being received inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a Tory is a member of Britain's right-wing Conservative Party
HE is His Excellency, an ambassador's title

explanation.surface: A diplomat is fooled by a conservative's conjecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' suggests being deceived; here it means being placed inside. Ambassadors are addressed as His or Her Excellency.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is an idea or hypothesis put forward to explain something, a supposition.

clue.text: Garden plant, soft and hairy, spread

indicators.note: spread out means scattered about, so the letters are laid out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A garden shrub with downy, fuzzy growth sprawls across the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsythia is a shrub grown in gardens for its bright yellow flowers in early spring.

clue.text: Woman, a prude, almost 50

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
a prig is a self-righteous, prudish person
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A strait-laced lady who is nearly fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: April is a female first name, so it can stand for a woman.

clue.text: What happens a few days from now, all the time?

definitions.text: What happens a few days from now
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: at New Year one year comes in and the old one goes out, which was days away when the puzzle appeared
second meaning: an idiom for continually, every year without change

explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared just before New Year, so the first part is a cryptic reading of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means constantly or repeatedly over a long period, while literally it describes the changing of the calendar year.

clue.text: Son, of course, shows pluck

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
natch is slang short for 'naturally', meaning of course

explanation.surface: A proud parent remarks that their boy naturally shows courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pluck' reads as the noun for courage, but it is the verb: to grab or pull quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To pluck something is to seize it with a quick tug, which is exactly what grabbing it away does.

clue.text: Small number interfering? Without a shadow of a doubt

definitions.text: Without a shadow of a doubt

parts.note: No. is the short form of number
messing with something is meddling or interfering

explanation.surface: A minor figure keeps meddling, and that is certain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' indicates the abbreviation, not a tiny quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase is used to insist that something is honestly and absolutely true.

clue.text: Small drink? A litre in all!

definitions.note: the answer is adjective or noun; 'in all' is an adverbial phrase meaning in total

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for litre

explanation.surface: A drinker protests that a small tipple adds up to a whole litre.
explanation.definitionFit: A total is the sum when everything is counted together, the amount altogether.

clue.text: Short durable cape — that's the gear

indicators.note: cut short means losing the end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: hard-wearing things are durable
a ness is a headland, as in place names like Orford Ness

explanation.surface: A hard-wearing cloak, shorter than usual, is the right kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cape' looks like a garment, but it is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A harness is the set of straps and fittings, or tack, used on a horse or climber: equipment.

clue.text: Faux pas made by enfant terrible losing face

indicators.note: a face is the front of something, so losing it means dropping the opening letter

parts.note: an enfant terrible is a little terror, an unruly person

explanation.surface: A notorious troublemaker commits a social blunder and is publicly embarrassed.
explanation.definitionFit: A faux pas is a social slip or blunder, a mistake in conduct.

clue.text: College one attended with girl friend, right?

parts.note: Alma is a girl's name
a mate is a friend
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone checks that they went to university alongside a girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'nourishing mother', the phrase names the school or university a person once studied at.

clue.text: Poor stewardship — mates naming me, unfortunately

indicators.note: something that has gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters fall out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boss complains of bad running of things when colleagues point the finger at him.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewardship is the managing of something in one's care, so doing it badly is bungled administration.

clue.text: Writer's payments from splendid connections

parts.note: royal can mean magnificent, fit for a king
ties are links or bonds

explanation.surface: An author earns money thanks to well-placed friends in high society.
explanation.definitionFit: Authors receive a percentage of book sales, paid as regular sums to the rights holder.

clue.text: Get the answers to only about five

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: sole means one and only
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A quiz-taker manages to crack only around five questions.
explanation.definitionFit: To work out a puzzle or problem is to find its answers, as solvers do here.

clue.text: Willing groups flushing out game

parts.note: happy to do something means willing to
families are groups of related things

explanation.surface: Eager beaters drive birds out of cover on a shooting day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flushing out game' paints a shoot, but here game is a pastime: in the card game, players draw out cards from others to complete their sets of families.
explanation.definitionFit: The children's card game has players ask opponents for named cards, prising them out to collect complete sets of four relatives.

clue.text: Wallaby in lane — moped crashed

indicators.note: a crashed vehicle is wrecked and jumbled, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A small kangaroo is caught on a country road after a scooter accident.
explanation.definitionFit: The pademelon is a small forest-dwelling wallaby of Australia and New Guinea.

clue.text: Awkward guy — one everyone sent up at first

indicators.note: at first says these pieces are placed at the start, ahead of the opening word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in a down clue sending something up means reading it from bottom to top

parts.note: all means everyone
to guy someone is to mock or rib them

explanation.surface: A clumsy fellow whom everybody mocked to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a noun for a man, but it is the verb meaning to ridicule. The clue's first-listed piece goes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Being uncomfortable and embarrassed in a situation makes one feel awkward.

clue.text: Newspaper backer shows spirit

parts.note: The Guardian is a British daily newspaper
an angel is a financial backer, especially of a theatre show

explanation.surface: A press baron's investor displays real courage.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardian angel is a protecting spirit believed to watch over a particular person.

clue.text: Leader of group of us met a connoisser of good food

indicators.note: the leader is whatever comes at the front, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
our means belonging to us
taken as written

explanation.surface: The head of our dining club was introduced to a food expert.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue misspells connoisseur as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmet is a person with a discerning palate who appreciates fine cuisine.

clue.text: Drink that's useful after last of exercises

indicators.note: after says the earlier-named piece follows the later one in the answer
the last of something is its final element, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
handy means useful or convenient

explanation.surface: A refreshing drink comes in handy once the workout is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A shandy is beer mixed with lemonade or ginger beer, a popular British drink.

clue.text: Deactivate part of lunar module

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is used, sitting inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: An astronaut switches off a section of the Apollo landing craft.
explanation.definitionFit: To unarm a weapon or device is to disable it, making it unable to fire or function.

clue.text: Runs after a boy responsible for fire-raising

indicators.note: after places the first-named piece behind the one mentioned next

parts.note: taken as written
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A lad who flees the scene is blamed for starting the blaze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' looks like a verb of fleeing, but it is cricket shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire-raising is the British legal term for deliberately setting fire to property, the crime of arson.

clue.text: Send a delivery too far along line

parts.note: over as a prefix means excessively, beyond the limit
a sales pitch is a salesman's line

explanation.surface: A courier takes a parcel past its destination down the road.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler delivers the ball; to overpitch is to bowl it too full, landing too near the batsman, so 'too far' supplies both the prefix and the fault.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a bowler sends down a delivery; overpitching is bowling it so it lands too far up the pitch.

clue.text: Food served up by Dad's Army

parts.note: Pa is Dad, so Dad's is Pa's
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Meals dished out by the Home Guard platoon of the classic British sitcom.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army is a BBC comedy about the wartime Home Guard; splitting the title gives the pieces. 'Served up' is not a reversal here.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta, such as spaghetti or penne, is a staple Italian food made from durum wheat dough.

clue.text: Shrubby plant that may be taken down shortly

definitions.text: Shrubby plant that may be taken down shortly

parts.note: surface reading: a bush that a gardener might cut down soon

parts.words: that may be taken down shortly
parts.note: setter's reading: a Christmas decoration that will come down in early January, as the puzzle appeared before the holiday ended

explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken down' suggests felling, but the plant is hung up as a festive decoration and removed soon after Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: This parasitic evergreen shrub, with white berries, is hung indoors at Christmas for kissing under and removed by Twelfth Night.

clue.text: Spring in a European country

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
taken as written

explanation.surface: Springtime spent in a continental country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' reads as the season, but it is a source of water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iberian kingdom with Madrid as capital is a European nation.

clue.text: A rent payer in shelter penning a note

indicators.note: to pen is to shut in an enclosure, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a tent is a canvas shelter
taken as written
n. is the abbreviation for note, as in footnote references

explanation.surface: A lodger living under canvas jots down a quick message.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant occupies property owned by a landlord and pays rent for it.

clue.text: Hear evidence about old disaster

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes round the second

parts.note: a judge hears evidence when trying a case
aged means old

explanation.surface: A court weighs testimony concerning a historic catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedy is a terrible event causing great suffering, a calamity.
